Frances Nunziata.bio: Frances Nunziata has represented York South—Weston on Toronto City Council since 1997, making her the longest-serving member of council. Before amalgamation she was elected a City of York school board trustee in 1985, a York city councillor in 1988, and Mayor of York from 1994 to 1997. She has been elected Speaker of Toronto City Council by her colleagues since December 2010.
Frances Nunziata.name: Frances Nunziata

promises.text: Make street safety in York South-Weston her number one priority, including tackling road congestion, working with Toronto Police, speaking out about gun violence, pushing for better parks and community spaces, and cleaner streets.

Champion youth priorities: continue work on the Mayor's Youth Safety Task Force, host youth job fairs, and advocate for free, accessible youth-focused recreational space and programs in York South-Weston.

Paul Ainslie.bio: Paul Ainslie was first elected to Toronto City Council in 2006 (appointed to a vacant Ward 41 seat in February 2006, then elected in Ward 43 that October), and has represented Scarborough—Guildwood as Ward 24 since 2018. He has over 25 years of experience across federal, provincial, and municipal government and previously owned and operated a small business. In May 2025 he was appointed Deputy Mayor for Scarborough.
Paul Ainslie.name: Paul Ainslie

promises.text: Deliver public transit improvements for Scarborough, including an LRT along Kingston Road and Morningside Avenue — City funding secured, with work toward a commitment from the Province and Federal governments for their share.
Build a Jobs Skills Centre in Scarborough at the former site of Sir Robert L. Borden BTI (200 Poplar Road) to train residents for long-term, good-paying jobs in the community.
On public safety: introduce a 'seize and destroy' motion demanding the Province amend the law so seized illegal weapons are destroyed rather than put back on the streets.

Michael Thompson.bio: Michael Thompson was first elected to Toronto City Council in 2003 and is now in his sixth term representing Scarborough Centre. Before entering politics he worked as an entrepreneur in the business and financial services sector (after serving as an assistant to Councillor Lorenzo Berardinetti, 1998-2003), and holds a BA in Economics from Concordia University. During the 2022 election he was charged with two counts of sexual assault and stepped down as deputy mayor and Chair of the Economic and Community Development Committee; he pleaded not guilty and was found not guilty on both charges in September 2025. He did not leave office and continues to serve his term.
Michael Thompson.name: Michael Thompson

Gord Perks.bio: First elected to Toronto City Council in 2006 to represent Ward 14 Parkdale—High Park; has represented Ward 4 Parkdale—High Park since the 2018 ward amalgamation and was re-elected in 2022. Before council, he worked in the environmental movement from 1987 to 2005 with Pollution Probe, Greenpeace Canada, the Better Transportation Coalition and the Toronto Environmental Alliance; he is the principal author of the Canadian Green Consumer Guide, a former Eye Weekly environment columnist, and a former adjunct professor with the University of Toronto's Environmental Studies department. In April 2026 he announced he will not seek re-election at the end of the 2022-2026 term.
committees: Toronto and East York Community Council
Gord Perks.name: Gord Perks

promises.text: Signed the Toronto Environmental Alliance's Greener City for All election pledge in 2022, committing to support priority actions including fully funding Toronto's climate strategy (2025/2030/2040 targets), overhauling heating and cooling bylaws and a fair stormwater charge for climate resilience, and regulations to eliminate unnecessary single-use items toward a zero-waste city.

Signed the Toronto Alliance to End Homelessness's Pledge to End Homelessness in 2022, committing to make ending homelessness through housing solutions a top City priority in the coming term, set minimum housing access targets for people experiencing homelessness, increase financial resources through a dedicated fund, and develop a Toronto Ending Homelessness Plan.

Paula Fletcher.bio: First elected to Toronto City Council in 2003 to represent the former Ward 30; re-elected in 2018 and 2022 to represent Ward 14 Toronto—Danforth. Before council she was elected as a Toronto District School Board trustee in 2000 and was a leader in the East End Parent Network; she has served as Deputy Speaker of City Council since August 2023 and as Chair of the Infrastructure and Environment Committee since May 2025. On August 19, 2026 she announced she will retire from politics at the end of the 2022-2026 term and will not seek re-election.
committees: Toronto and East York Community Council
Paula Fletcher.name: Paula Fletcher

promises.text: Signed the Toronto Environmental Alliance's Greener City for All election pledge in 2022, committing to support priority actions including fully funding Toronto's climate strategy (2025/2030/2040 targets), overhauling heating and cooling bylaws and a fair stormwater charge for climate resilience, and regulations to eliminate unnecessary single-use items toward a zero-waste city.

Signed the Toronto Alliance to End Homelessness's Pledge to End Homelessness in 2022, committing to make ending homelessness through housing solutions a top City priority in the coming term, set minimum housing access targets for people experiencing homelessness, increase financial resources through a dedicated fund, and develop a Toronto Ending Homelessness Plan.

Anthony Perruzza.bio: Serving on Toronto City Council since 2006, representing Ward 8 York West from 2006 to 2018 and Ward 7 Humber River-Black Creek since the 2018 ward amalgamation, re-elected in 2022. Earlier he was a trustee on the Metro Toronto Separate School Board (1985-88), a North York city councillor (1988-90), and a Member of Provincial Parliament for Downsview (1990-95); he ran for mayor of Toronto in the 2023 by-election. He is seeking re-election in the 2026 municipal election.
Anthony Perruzza.name: Anthony Perruzza

promises.text: Signed the Toronto Environmental Alliance's Greener City for All election pledge in 2022, committing to support priority actions including fully funding Toronto's climate strategy (2025/2030/2040 targets), overhauling heating and cooling bylaws and a fair stormwater charge for climate resilience, and regulations to eliminate unnecessary single-use items toward a zero-waste city.

In his 2026 re-election campaign, his stated priorities are affordability, continued investment in infrastructure, essential services and value for taxpayers, with focus on roads, sewers, parks, playgrounds, transit, housing and support for seniors.

Shelley Carroll.bio: Shelley Carroll was first elected to Toronto City Council in 2003, representing Ward 33 Don Valley East; she had previously served as a Toronto District School Board trustee from 2000 to 2003. She resigned from council in April 2018 to run as the Ontario Liberal candidate in the Don Valley North provincial election, then returned to council after winning the newly formed Ward 17 in the 2018 municipal election, and was re-elected in 2022. She served as Chair of the Budget Committee under both Mayor John Tory and Mayor Olivia Chow, and became Chair of the Toronto Police Services Board in January 2025.
Shelley Carroll.name: Shelley Carroll

promises.text: Open a constituency office located within Ward 17, Don Valley North, so residents can meet their councillor in person within the ward rather than at a civic centre.
Continue working with the community to build a Don Valley North that is "liveable and affordable for generations to come."

James Pasternak.bio: James Pasternak was first elected to Toronto City Council in 2010, representing Ward 10 York Centre; he had previously served as a Toronto District School Board trustee from 2006 to 2010. He has represented Ward 6 York Centre since the 2018 ward boundary changes, and was re-elected in 2014, 2018 and 2022. He holds degrees from York University, the University of Western Ontario, and the London School of Economics and Political Science.
James Pasternak.name: James Pasternak

promises.text: Commit to responsible budgeting while expanding affordable housing options and easing the cost of living for Ward 6 families.
Improve city parks, recreation programs, and services for seniors so every resident can thrive in the Ward 6 community.

Josh Matlow.bio: Josh Matlow was first elected to Toronto City Council in 2010, representing Ward 22 St. Paul's; he had previously served as a Toronto District School Board trustee from 2003 to 2010, and before that was co-director of Earthroots, a Toronto-based environmental organization. He has represented Ward 12 Toronto—St. Paul's since the 2018 ward boundary changes, and was re-elected in 2014, 2018 and 2022. He ran for Mayor of Toronto in the 2023 mayoral by-election while continuing to serve as a councillor.
committees: Toronto and East York Community Council
Josh Matlow.name: Josh Matlow

promises.text: Demand a public inquiry into the Eglinton LRT construction delays and cost overruns.
Open Old City Hall to the public and create a Museum of Toronto there.

Jaye Robinson.bio: Jaye Robinson (1962-2024) was first elected to Toronto City Council in 2010 and re-elected in 2014, 2018 and 2022, serving Don Valley West for nearly 14 years. Before entering municipal politics, she spent more than 20 years as a city civil servant, including as the City of Toronto's Director of Special Events, where she helped launch Nuit Blanche, Summerlicious and Winterlicious. She served as Chair of the Public Works and Infrastructure Committee (2014-2018), where she introduced Toronto's first Vision Zero Road Safety Plan, and as Chair of the Toronto Transit Commission (2018-2022). She died in office on May 16, 2024, after being diagnosed with breast cancer in 2019; the seat was filled by Rachel Chernos Lin in the November 2024 by-election.
Jaye Robinson.name: Jaye Robinson

promises.text: Pledged to keep the next council focused on better delivery of core municipal services such as snow clearance, pothole repair and garbage pick-up, arguing 'the next City Council's focus should be on providing better value to Toronto taxpayers.'
Pledged support for open tendering of city contracts as a fiscal measure, stating it 'would have saved $12-48 million per year' on taxes and spending.

Signed the Toronto Environmental Alliance's 'Greener City for All' election pledge, committing to actions toward Toronto's 2025, 2030 and 2040 climate targets, including fully funding the city's climate strategy and accelerating investments in affordable housing, transit and green jobs.

Gary Crawford.bio: Gary Crawford was first elected to Toronto City Council in 2010, succeeding Brian Ashton in Scarborough Southwest, and re-elected in 2014, 2018 and 2022. Previously he served as a Toronto District School Board trustee (2003-2010) and worked as a professional artist and part-time musician before entering politics. As Mayor John Tory's budget chief from 2014 to 2023, he chaired the city's Budget Committee for nine years. He resigned from council in July 2023 to run as the Ontario Progressive Conservative candidate in the Scarborough—Guildwood provincial by-election and was defeated by Liberal candidate Andrea Hazell; his council seat was filled by Parthi Kandavel in the November 2023 by-election.
Gary Crawford.name: Gary Crawford

promises.text: Ran on a platform centred on affordability, including keeping city spending under control as the city's long-serving budget chief.
Ran on a platform centred on community safety as a core priority for Scarborough Southwest.
Ran on a platform centred on 'maintaining the integrity of single-family homes,' pledging to protect the character of established residential neighbourhoods in Scarborough Southwest.

Vincent Crisanti.bio: Vincent Crisanti (born 1953) worked as an advertising and signage sales manager before entering municipal politics; he served as an Etobicoke city councillor before amalgamation in 1995. He was elected to Toronto City Council in 2010, re-elected in 2014, served as Deputy Mayor for Etobicoke (2014-2017), lost his seat to Michael Ford in 2018, and returned to council in the October 2022 election, winning Ward 1 Etobicoke North with 41% of the vote. He currently serves on the city's Audit Committee and the Planning and Housing Committee, sits on the Board of Governors of Exhibition Place, and is the City's Seniors Advocate.
Vincent Crisanti.name: Vincent Crisanti

promises.text: Pledged to improve city infrastructure by encouraging investment in road resurfacing and sidewalk work in Etobicoke North.
Pledged to push for improvements to the public realm, including upgrades to public parks and community centres.

Pledged to set an agreement in motion for a light rail extension that would extend the train route from Humber College to a new GO Station at Belfield and Highway 27, consistent with his long-standing advocacy for extending the Finch West LRT to the Etobicoke North GO Station.

Stephen Holyday.bio: Stephen Holyday has been Toronto's councillor for Etobicoke Centre since December 2014, serving Ward 3 from 2014-2018 and Ward 2 since the 2018 boundary changes; he was re-elected in 2022 with 72.28% of the vote. Before entering politics he spent 15 years (1999-2014) as a manager at the Ontario Ministry of Energy, and he holds a Bachelor of Technology in Architectural Science from Ryerson University. He is the son of Doug Holyday, a former Etobicoke mayor and Ward 3 councillor, and previously served as Deputy Mayor (2017, and again 2018-2022).
Stephen Holyday.name: Stephen Holyday

promises.text: Reduce traffic congestion in Etobicoke Centre.
Invest in transit infrastructure to serve the growing population.

Jon Burnside.bio: Jon Burnside was elected councillor for Ward 16, Don Valley East, in the 2022 municipal election, returning to City Hall after previously representing Ward 26, Don Valley West, from 2014-2018 (a seat he lost when wards were redrawn). He served as a Toronto Police officer from 1991 to 2001 and later founded and operated a healthy food delivery business in the GTA for about 14 years. He chaired the TTC from November 2022 to August 2023.
Jon Burnside.name: Jon Burnside

promises.text: Open a local community office in the ward. (Office opened at 895 Lawrence Ave E, Suite 205.)
Hold in-person Open Houses for development applications before the City's virtual consultations. (15 held.)
Add officers to Toronto Police community policing and step up local patrols.

Brad Bradford.bio: Brad Bradford has been the councillor for Ward 19, Beaches-East York, since first being elected in 2018, winning re-election in 2022 with 54.71% of the vote. Before entering politics he worked as an urban planner, including stakeholder engagement in the office of then-chief planner Jennifer Keesmaat; he holds a Bachelor of Environmental Studies from York University and a master's in urban planning from the University of Waterloo. He chaired the Planning and Housing Committee from 2022 to August 2023 and later served as its vice-chair; he is a candidate in the 2026 Toronto mayoral election.
committees: Toronto and East York Community Council
Brad Bradford.name: Brad Bradford

promises.text: Bring more housing to Beaches-East York and across the city.
Pursue road safety projects that save lives.
Support main streets and small businesses so they thrive.

Mike Colle.bio: Mike Colle has represented Ward 8, Eglinton-Lawrence on Toronto City Council since December 2018 and was re-elected in 2022 with 70.3% of the vote; he has served as Deputy Mayor for North York since August 2023. Before joining council he was the Liberal MPP for Eglinton-Lawrence from 1995 to 2018, serving as a cabinet minister under Premier Dalton McGuinty. Earlier in his career he was a councillor for the City of York and Metropolitan Toronto, TTC chair from 1988 to 1994, and a high school history and economics teacher.
Mike Colle.name: Mike Colle

promises.text: Increase the supply of affordable housing through the Lawrence Heights Revitalization, the Reena residence, the Shortt Street parking lot proposal, and inclusionary zoning in all new developments.
Expand Mobile Mental Health Crisis Response Teams to respond to mental health and substance abuse emergencies, including fentanyl poisonings in the Eglinton-Marlee area.
Increase neighbourhood policing to combat gun crimes, carjackings, hate crimes, and deal with traffic enforcement.

Jennifer McKelvie.bio: Jennifer McKelvie represented Ward 25, Scarborough—Rouge Park on Toronto City Council from 2018 until she resigned on May 9, 2025, having been re-elected in 2022 with 72.3% of the vote. A professional geoscientist with a PhD in geology from the University of Toronto, she previously managed research partnerships at the Nuclear Waste Management Organization and the Canadian Institute for Advanced Research. She served as Deputy Mayor of Toronto (2022-2023) and as chair of the Infrastructure and Environment Committee; she left council after being elected as the Liberal Member of Parliament for Ajax in the April 28, 2025 federal election.
committees: Board of Directors of Toronto Hydro
Jennifer McKelvie.name: Jennifer McKelvie

promises.text: Advance the Eglinton East LRT as a service-first priority for Scarborough.
Tackle basement flooding affecting Scarborough homes.
Protect ravines and manage growth responsibly.

Nick Mantas.bio: Nick Mantas has represented Ward 22, Scarborough-Agincourt on Toronto City Council since winning a by-election on January 15, 2021 (sworn in January 18), replacing Jim Karygiannis; he was re-elected in 2022. He holds a BA in economics from York University and previously worked as a federal constituency assistant, a policy advisor to the Senate of Canada, and chief of staff to former Ward 22 councillor Jim Karygiannis. He has also served as chair of the Panarcadian Federation of Canada and as a director of the Hellenic Canadian Board of Trade.
Nick Mantas.name: Nick Mantas

promises.text: Bring traffic-calming measures to schools in the ward.
Increase community safety in Scarborough-Agincourt.
Extend the Line 4 Sheppard subway into Scarborough.

Neethan Shan.bio: Neethan Shan was elected to Toronto City Council in a by-election on September 29, 2025, succeeding Jennifer McKelvie, who resigned mid-term on May 9, 2025 after being elected to the House of Commons. He previously served as Toronto's first Tamil-Canadian city councillor for Ward 42 Scarborough—Rouge River from 2017 to 2018, and as a Toronto District School Board trustee (2016–2017 and 2022–2025, serving as Board Chair from 2024 to 2025). Born in Jaffna, Sri Lanka, he arrived in Canada as a refugee at age 16 and previously worked as a teacher, youth outreach worker, and executive director of the Urban Alliance on Race Relations.
Neethan Shan.name: Neethan Shan

promises.text: Fight for the transit Scarborough needs and support a regional transit plan specific to Scarborough.
Ensure community voices are heard at City Hall and that neighbourhood associations play a key role in development decisions affecting their communities.
Protect local businesses displaced by development and ensure local city projects support local businesses and create local jobs.

Jamaal Myers.bio: Jamaal Myers was first elected to Toronto City Council on October 24, 2022 and took office November 15, 2022, filling the Ward 23 seat after the sudden death of incumbent Cynthia Lai days before the election. Before entering politics he worked as a corporate lawyer, most recently as senior legal counsel at TD Bank focusing on environmental, social and governance matters. Born and raised in Scarborough in Toronto Community Housing, he holds a BA from the University of Western Ontario, an MSc from the London School of Economics, and a JD from New York University.
Jamaal Myers.name: Jamaal Myers

promises.text: Legalize and regulate rooming houses and work toward building 40,000 affordable rental homes in Toronto by 2030.
Oppose TTC service cuts, support bus lanes in Scarborough to help with traffic, and lower TTC fares.
Make the TTC free for seniors and students, and allow free transfers between TTC buses and GO Transit in Scarborough following the Scarborough LRT closure.

Alejandra Bravo.bio: Alejandra Bravo was first elected to Toronto City Council on October 24, 2022, taking office November 15, 2022 with over 70 percent of the vote in the open-seat race to succeed Ana Bailão. She previously ran for council in Davenport in 2003, 2006 and 2014, and was the federal NDP candidate in Davenport in 2021. Born in Chile in 1971, she moved to Canada with her family as a refugee as a child; she was Director of Leadership and Training at the Broadbent Institute and spent a decade as Manager of Leadership and Learning at the Maytree Foundation.
committees: Toronto and East York Community Council
Alejandra Bravo.name: Alejandra Bravo

promises.text: End exclusionary zoning, waive City permits and fees to support new affordable housing, and create a dedicated planning team to expedite permits and approvals.
Ensure City-owned land is used to build new mixed-income affordable housing communities.
Fight for stronger protections from renovictions and unfair rent increases, and advocate for a local bylaw setting a maximum allowable temperature in all apartments.

Ausma Malik.bio: Ausma Malik was elected to Toronto City Council in October 2022 and took office on November 15, 2022, representing Ward 10 Spadina–Fort York, succeeding Joe Cressy. She previously served as a Toronto District School Board trustee from 2014 to 2018, where she helped get Jean Lumb Public School built, and was Director of Advocacy and Organizing at the Atkinson Foundation from 2016 to 2022. The first hijab-wearing Muslim woman elected to public office in Canada, she was appointed Statutory Deputy Mayor and Deputy Mayor for Toronto and East York by Mayor Olivia Chow in August 2023.
committees: Toronto and East York Community Council
Ausma Malik.name: Ausma Malik

promises.text: End exclusionary zoning to get more higher-density housing built across the city, and support sustainable infill construction to jump-start the development of more housing supply.
Utilize city-owned sites for new affordable, rental, and non-profit housing developments, and identify more opportunities to collaborate with non-profit partners and Toronto Community Housing.
Increase the Vacant Home Tax to discourage speculative buyers.

Lily Cheng.bio: Lily Cheng was elected to Toronto City Council in October 2022 and took office on November 15, 2022, representing Ward 18 Willowdale, succeeding the retiring John Filion (she had previously run against Filion in 2018). A Willowdale resident for over a dozen years, she is a community organizer who founded North York Moms, co-founded We Love Willowdale after the 2018 Yonge Street van attack, spearheaded the Willowdale Covid Response Network, and served as executive director of the NeighbourLink North York food bank.
Lily Cheng.name: Lily Cheng

promises.text: Fight for a Cummer subway station at Yonge and Cummer to serve Willowdale residents, a promise she made in her campaign platform.
Advocate for smaller-scale supportive housing and mixed-income and modular housing, and support the regulation of rooming houses.
Improve the community consultation process so that it considers non-English speaking members of the community and better addresses public safety and the loss of green space.

Dianne Saxe.bio: Dianne Saxe was elected to Toronto City Council in October 2022 and took office on November 15, 2022, representing Ward 11 University—Rosedale, succeeding Mike Layton. An environmental and energy lawyer, she was Ontario's third and last Environmental Commissioner (2015–2019) before the office was abolished, and served as Deputy Leader of the Green Party of Ontario from 2020 to 2022 before resigning to run as an independent. She sits on Council as an independent and serves as the Mayor's Environmental Champion. Ahead of the October 26, 2026 municipal election, she withdrew her Ward 11 re-election candidacy in August 2026 and registered instead in Ward 14 Toronto—Danforth following Paula Fletcher's retirement announcement.
committees: Toronto and East York Community Council
Dianne Saxe.name: Dianne Saxe

promises.text: Enforce a Vacant Home Tax to reduce speculators.
Build the city "in and up," mitigating urban sprawl with more middle housing in all residential zones.
Fund a revolving loan fund for non-profit housing providers.

Amber Morley.bio: Amber Morley was elected to represent Ward 3, Etobicoke—Lakeshore on October 24, 2022, defeating incumbent Mark Grimes with 46.44% of the vote. Before council she spent over 20 years in community advocacy, including as Director of the South Etobicoke Youth Assembly at LAMP Community Health Centre, as an Administrative Assistant to Councillor Peter Milczyn, and as a Constituency Assistant for Ward 4 Etobicoke-Centre. She also serves as a non-statutory Deputy Mayor for Etobicoke and York, appointed August 2023.
Amber Morley.name: Amber Morley

promises.text: Push for a set standard of affordable units in all new housing developments, and lend support to new co-operative housing initiatives.
Utilize city-owned land for affordable housing developments, and work with other levels of government to leverage provincial and federal lands.
Commit to a Vacant Home Tax to discourage speculative buyers.

Chris Moise.bio: Chris Moise was elected as City Councillor for Ward 13, Toronto Centre on October 24, 2022, winning 48.48% of the vote (10,457 votes). He previously served six years as a Toronto District School Board Trustee (including as vice-chair), worked as an addictions counsellor at St. Michael's Hospital for 22 years and as a police officer in Waterloo, and has run a small business in the St. Lawrence Neighbourhood for over 17 years.
committees: Toronto and East York Community Council
Chris Moise.name: Chris Moise

promises.text: Encourage the construction of all housing types -- multiplexes, high-rises, and public, market, and transitional housing -- to make Toronto a safe space for all.
Address the interconnected nature of the housing, mental health, and addiction crises.
Work with post-secondary institutions to help housing accessibility for students on and around campus.

Olivia Chow.bio: Olivia Chow was elected the 66th Mayor of Toronto in the June 26, 2023 mayoral by-election and assumed office on July 12, 2023, becoming the first person of Asian descent and the first woman since amalgamation to hold the office. Her political career includes serving as a Toronto school board trustee (1985-1991), a Metro/Toronto city councillor for Trinity-Spadina (1992-2005), and as the NDP Member of Parliament for Trinity-Spadina (2006-2014). She immigrated to Toronto from Hong Kong at age 13 and is the widow of former NDP leader Jack Layton.
Olivia Chow.name: Olivia Chow

promises.text: Build 25,000 rent-controlled homes over the next eight years on city-owned land, including at least 7,500 affordable units and at least 2,500 rent-geared-to-income units, with the city acting as developer.
Raise the Vacant Home Tax to 3% and use the funds collected to construct affordable and subsidized units and support the City's existing affordable housing initiatives, including rent supplements.

Create a Toronto Renters Action Committee, a task force dedicated to establishing anti-renoviction bylaws, advocating for real rent control, and reviewing existing policies and programs related to renters.

Olivia Chow.ward: Mayor of Toronto (city-wide); formerly Councillor for Ward 20, Trinity-Spadina (1998-2005)

Parthi Kandavel.bio: Parthi Kandavel was elected to Toronto City Council in a by-election on November 30, 2023, replacing Gary Crawford. Between 2014 and 2022 he served as a TDSB trustee for Scarborough Southwest; he previously worked for twelve years as an elementary school teacher and holds a BA in Mathematics and Political Science from the University of Waterloo.
Parthi Kandavel.name: Parthi Kandavel

promises.text: Increase the number of daycare and childcare spaces in Scarborough Southwest.
Build more road safety infrastructure in the ward.
Push for better transit, more affordable housing, complete communities, and more transparent local government decision making.

Rachel Chernos Lin.bio: Rachel Chernos Lin won the Ward 15 by-election on November 4, 2024, succeeding the late Jaye Robinson. She previously served as a Toronto District School Board trustee for six years (2018-2024), including two years as TDSB Chair. She holds an Honours BA from the University of Toronto and a Master's degree in History from Brown University, and is a published historian.
Rachel Chernos Lin.name: Rachel Chernos Lin

promises.text: Manage development responsibly so neighbourhoods stay liveable, push for unit sizes that suit residents, and advocate for more affordable housing near transit plus complete communities with parks, recreation, and local childcare.

Fight gridlock with a multi-pronged approach: modern signal technology, fewer long-term lane closures by developers, traffic monitors, safer and more efficient transit, and pedestrian safety under Vision Zero.
Strengthen community safety by addressing home invasions, auto theft and gun violence, and supporting the five-year plan to hire 500 additional police officers while bringing down response times.

John Tory.bio: John Tory served as the 65th Mayor of Toronto from December 2014 to February 2023, elected in 2014 and re-elected in 2018 and 2022. He resigned on February 17, 2023, after acknowledging a relationship with a staff member. A lawyer by training, he previously led the Progressive Conservative Party of Ontario (2004-2009), served as an MPP, worked as a broadcaster with CFRB, and held executive roles with Rogers Communications.
committees: Toronto Police Services Board (member by virtue of office)
Exhibition Place Board of Governors (member by virtue of office)
John Tory.name: John Tory

promises.text: Introduce a five-point housing plan: seek provincial authority for a 'use it or lose it' policy against idle developers, allow more missing-middle housing (laneway and garden suites) with development-charge exemptions for buildings of four units or fewer, create a Development and Growth Division as a one-stop development review shop, improve incentives for purpose-built rental housing, and grant a portion of city-owned land to non-profit developers.
Create 40,000 affordable rental units over 12 years (averaging about 3,300 per year), while keeping property tax increases capped at the rate of inflation or lower.

Advance a transit plan including a $586 million investment to add 60 new streetcars to the TTC fleet, launch the first RapidTO bus-only corridor on Eglinton East, introduce free two-hour TTC transfers and a Fair Pass discount for low-income riders, and maintain the TTC's large electric bus fleet.

John Tory.ward: Former Mayor of Toronto (city-wide), December 2014 – February 2023; resigned February 17, 2023
